claim: An FSx for Windows File Server file system is joined to an Active Directory domain, either AWS Managed Microsoft AD or a self-managed Microsoft Active Directory; Amazon FSx does not support AD Connector or Simple AD.
question: Which directory types can FSx for Windows File Server join, and which can it not use?

values.display: Using a self-managed Microsoft Active Directory

qualifiers.scope: FSx for Windows File Server Active Directory integration

evidence.quote: Amazon FSx does not support [Active Directory Connector](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directoryservice/latest/admin-guide/directory_ad_connector.html) and [Simple Active Directory](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directoryservice/latest/admin-guide/directory_simple_ad.html).

Amazon FSx provides two options using your FSx for Windows File Server file system with Active Directory: [Using Amazon FSx with AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory](fsx-aws-managed-ad.md) and [Using a self-managed Microsoft Active Directory](self-managed-AD.md).

claim: Simple AD is a standalone managed directory powered by a Samba 4 Active Directory Compatible Server that offers a subset of AWS Managed Microsoft AD features; it does not support MFA, trusts with other domains, PowerShell, the AD recycle bin, group managed service accounts or schema extensions for POSIX and Microsoft applications.
question: How does Simple AD compare with AWS Managed Microsoft AD?

values.display: a subset of the features offered by AWS Managed Microsoft AD

evidence.quote: Simple AD is a standalone managed directory that is powered by a Samba 4 Active Directory Compatible Server.

However, note that Simple AD does not support features such as multi-factor authentication (MFA), trust relationships with other domains, Active Directory Administrative Center, PowerShell support, Active Directory recycle bin, group managed service accounts, and schema extensions for POSIX and Microsoft applications.

Simple AD provides a subset of the features offered by AWS Managed Microsoft AD, including the ability to manage user accounts and group memberships, create and apply group policies, securely connect to Amazon EC2 instances, and provide Kerberos-based single sign-on (SSO).
